system.name: XKD
system.one_liner: Self-supervised audio-video learning: masked autoencoders per modality, then cross-modal teacher-student distillation after aligning the two feature domains.

content.variant_note: mirrored video and audio branches; three objectives (reconstruction, domain alignment, distillation) drawn as colour-coded arrows between feature distributions
content.argues: Video and audio can teach each other: after aligning their feature domains, each modality's student is distilled from the other modality's teacher, on top of masked reconstruction.
content.subject: Mirrored audio and video autoencoder-student and teacher branches with feature distributions linked by distillation and alignment arrows.

elements.name: video autoencoder (encoder + decoder) / audio autoencoder (encoder + decoder)
elements.role: reconstructs the highly masked input of one modality so the encoder learns modality-specific information
elements.drawn_as: italic label above a tall encoder box and a decoder box

elements.name: encoder
elements.role: shared by the autoencoder path and the student path, one per modality
elements.drawn_as: tall white rounded rectangle, rotated label, 0.75 pt black outline

elements.name: decoder
elements.role: reconstructs the masked input from the encoder output
elements.drawn_as: tall white rounded rectangle, rotated label, beside the encoder

elements.name: head
elements.role: student head that turns the encoder output into the student feature
elements.drawn_as: small white rounded rectangle, rotated label, under the decoder

elements.name: video student (encoder + head) / audio student (encoder + head)
elements.role: student that is distilled from the cross-modal teacher
elements.drawn_as: italic label under the encoder and head

elements.name: f_s^v / f_s^a
elements.role: feature distribution of the video / audio student
elements.drawn_as: bell curve at the end of the student branch, grey-green and wide for video, pale for audio

elements.name: audio teacher (encoder + head) / video teacher (encoder + head)
elements.role: gives cross-modal supervision to the student of the opposite modality
elements.drawn_as: hatched grey encoder and head boxes followed by a white refine box

elements.name: refine
elements.role: feature refinement, one half of the domain-alignment step
elements.drawn_as: white rounded box with rotated label after each teacher head

elements.name: f_t^a / f_t^v
elements.drawn_as: narrow bell curve, pale for audio and darker for video

elements.name: masked reconstruction
elements.drawn_as: thick green arrow with a green italic label above each autoencoder, pointing along its data flow

elements.name: cross-modal knowledge distillation
elements.role: objective: each student distils from the cross-modal teacher
elements.drawn_as: two thick red curved arrows from teacher bell up to student bell, red italic labels

elements.name: domain alignment
elements.role: minimises the discrepancy between the video and audio feature distributions
elements.drawn_as: four short blue double-headed arrows beside the bells, blue italic labels between the halves

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each objective one saturated colour used on its arrow and on a same-colour italic label over a grey-and-black body, so the losses are told apart without a legend; mirror the two modalities so the cross-modal links meet in the centre.
lessons.suits: multi-objective self-supervised frameworks with two symmetric branches (two modalities, two views, teacher and student) where several losses tie together the same few features.

evidence: Masked reconstruction: autoencoders are used to learn representations from individual modalities through reconstruction of highly masked inputs.
two domains are aligned through feature refinement and minimizing domain discrepancies.
The students are used to distil knowledge from their respective cross-modal teachers.

summary: XKD is a self-supervised framework that learns video and audio representations together: each modality has a masked autoencoder, and the student of one modality is distilled from the teacher of the other after a domain-alignment step. The figure draws this as a mirrored 2x2 layout. Video flows left to right on the left and audio right to left on the right; the top tracks hold the masked autoencoder and student (encoder, decoder, head), the bottom tracks the hatched teachers with a refine box. Bell curves mark feature distributions, and three colours mark the three objectives: green reconstruction, blue domain alignment, red cross-modal distillation. Real frames and spectrograms of one sample clip appear in every view.
summary_zh: XKD 的总览图：视频与音频左右镜像排布，上排是带掩码重建的自编码器和学生网络，下排是斜线填充的教师网络；钟形曲线表示特征分布，绿、蓝、红三色分别标出掩码重建、域对齐和跨模态蒸馏，各视图都用同一段板球视频及其频谱图作样例。
notes: Kind kept as the prior (model-anatomy, objective-graph); the caption speaks of 3 steps but the figure shows them as simultaneous colour-coded objectives, not as a sequence, so stage-pipeline is not listed. The meaning of the hatched fill (teacher) and of the superscripts g and l (global and local view) is read from the drawing; the provided paper text does not define them. Picture counts are by eye (the digest counts 22 tiles; some sit under the masking grids). The bell glyphs are not vector fills, so their shades are described only in words.
